title.title: A domain with no small Cohen–Macaulay module
title.subtitle: Claim: a 3-dimensional complete normal local domain over $\mathbb{C}$ with no f.g. module of full depth

plain: A ring that cannot be made to look 'nice' by any finite module, though infinite ones exist

panels.axisLabel: the dimension of the complete local domain $R$

beats.text: A small Cohen–Macaulay module would settle several homological conjectures at once
In dimension at most 2 one always exists
The claim: in dimension 3 over $\mathbb{C}$, none does

steps: Suppose a finite module of full depth existed
Follow its Chern character on a resolution of an explicit surface
A numerical inequality rules it out

achievement.label: Hochster's small Cohen–Macaulay conjecture (1970s)
achievement.context: Counterexample: a branched cover of a blown-up plane, obstructed by a Chern-character inequality
achievement.note: Characteristic $p$ and mixed characteristic are not addressed

verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and the review; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Hochster asked if every complete local domain has a finite module of full depth.
A Chern character inequality on a resolution rules any such module out.
Claimed: a three-dimensional domain with none.

sources.quote: There is a 3-dimensional complete Noetherian normal local domain containing C, residue field C, with no nonzero finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay module (depth 3)
It is true in dimension at most 2
The char-p and mixed-char versions are not addressed. No Lean.
Characteristic $p$ is not addressed. It is 17 pages.
